# The stored image is the contract

## Context & decision

`ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` validated the file the person picked and
_then_ shrank it. The 5MB limit therefore measured the **Source File** while the
resize that would have made it ~400KB ran on the next line.

The fix is to decide what the limit is _about_. **The limit describes the
artifact we keep, not the artifact we are handed.** Size validation moves after
the resize, so it gates the **Receipt Image**; the Source File is bounded only by
a 25MB pre-decode ceiling that exists to protect the browser's memory, not to
judge the receipt. Everything follows from that principle:

- **2400px longest axis at 85% JPEG.** The stored image is what a person zooms
  into, so the pixel budget is chosen for human reading, not for OCR.
- **HEIC and PNG transcode to JPEG.** One stored format. PNG additionally never
  honoured the 85% quality argument (`toBlob` ignores it for lossless formats),
  so a PNG "resize" could return a file _larger_ than it arrived.
- **Zoom stops at the image's own natural resolution**, replacing a flat
  `MAX_ZOOM = 400`. 100% is fit-to-viewport, so a fixed percentage meant
  different things per device: on a phone 400% was roughly 1:1, on a desktop it
  demanded ~2.3× more detail than a 2000px file contains. The mush people saw at
  high zoom was the viewer promising pixels the resize had already discarded.
- **No backfill.** A per-image ceiling reads each generation correctly on its
  own. Re-resizing the pre-`901b670` full-resolution originals would destroy
  detail we already paid to store — so `/admin/resize-images` is deleted rather
  than updated, which also closes the **M2** finding (an unauthenticated
  delete-and-reupload page) instead of deferring it a fourth time.

## Considered options

- **Raise `MAX_IMAGE_MB` from 5 to ~15.** A one-line unblock, rejected because
  the gate would still measure the wrong artifact: a 16MB photo that resizes to
  400KB is still refused for no reason the family can perceive.
- **Keep the gate, improve the error message.** Cheapest, and the honest reading
  of it is "we have automated shrinking, and we are going to ask you to do it
  anyway."
- **Keep PNG lossless, add a keep-the-smaller-file guard.** Genuinely defensible
  — JPEG ringing around small glyphs is real, and screenshot receipts have sharp
  edges. Rejected for a single stored format; at 2400px and 85% the artefacts are
  well below the threshold that matters for reading a total.
- **Two artifacts per receipt** — a small display/OCR copy plus a large read
  copy. Best quality-per-byte, rejected as doubling the storage objects and
  adding a second signed-URL path to every surface that shows a receipt.
- **Cap zoom at ~1.5× native** rather than a hard 1:1, keeping some headroom
  because magnification past 1:1 still helps low-vision readers even though it
  adds no information. Rejected in favour of the stricter rule: every pixel on
  screen is a real pixel.

## Consequences

- **Transcoding is irreversible and lossy.** Detail discarded at upload never
  comes back — there is no original to re-derive from, by design. Revisiting the
  2400px/85% numbers only affects receipts uploaded after the change.
- **Zoom disappears for small images.** Anything already at or below viewport
  size has `MIN_ZOOM == MAX_ZOOM` and both controls sit disabled. Accepted
  deliberately over faking magnification.
- **A resize failure now becomes a rejection.** `prepareFileForUpload` falls back
  to the original on any error; a 12MB original then fails the post-resize gate.
  The file is refused either way, but the real reason is "we could not shrink
  it", and the message must say so rather than blaming the file's size.
- **The email path diverges.** The Resend handler uploads attachment bytes
  straight to storage with no size check and no resize (Deno — no Canvas), so an
  emailed receipt is stored full-size while the same receipt uploaded in the
  browser becomes 2400px JPEG. Resizing there needs a WASM image library and a
  second copy of these rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/`, kept in lock-step
  by hand. Logged in the [backlog](../product-backlog.md) rather than built.
- **Storage now holds three generations** of Receipt Image and always will. This
  is fine for zoom (see the "Zoom never invents pixels" invariant) but means
  storage-size statistics are not comparable across upload dates.

diff --git a/docs/product-backlog.md b/docs/product-backlog.md
index 4693f57..576ec90 100644
--- a/docs/product-backlog.md
+++ b/docs/product-backlog.md
@@ -17,13 +17,12 @@ reference, not a separate to-do list.
 - **Receipt image — rotate.** Rotate left and right anywhere a receipt is viewed.
 - **Profile — manage emails.** Let users add/edit the email addresses associated with their account. This interacts with the unverified-alias security item below — verification is the fix, so design them together.
 - **Family editor.** Let a user create a family and then invite other users to join it. Designed in [PRD — Family Invitations](prd-family-invitations.md) (invite-by-email + `SECURITY DEFINER` accept RPC; the sanctioned membership-write path that replaces the dropped self-insert policy). The read-only half already shipped — the Profile page lists family members via the `get_family_members()` RPC — so what remains is invite / accept / remove.
-- **iPhone camera / mobile capture.** Use the camera on an iPhone to take photos of receipts. Designed in [PRD — Mobile Capture](prd-mobile-capture.md): a single-purpose, chrome-free `/capture` route installed to the home screen as a PWA (`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`) — **not** a native iOS app, since the camera and photo library already work in mobile Safari and what's missing is a phone-shaped surface, not a capability. Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` behind a queued, immediately-re-arming shutter. Requires a route-group split of `src/routes/+layout.svelte` (auth gate out, nav chrome into `(app)`). Two open risks called out there: **standalone-mode session persistence** (spike before building on it) and **no offline capture on iOS** (Safari has no Background Sync — the one scenario that would justify going native). Also flags a suspected bug worth verifying on-device: the receipts `accept` list includes `image/heic`, which may make iOS hand over a raw HEIC that `resizeImage()` then skips entirely (`imageResize.ts:71`), sending a full-size photo to storage and Mistral on cellular. Addressed by the HEIC→JPEG transcode in [Receipt Image Resize & Zoom](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md), which still wants on-device confirmation of what iOS actually hands over.
+- **iPhone camera / mobile capture.** Use the camera on an iPhone to take photos of receipts. Designed in [PRD — Mobile Capture](prd-mobile-capture.md): a single-purpose, chrome-free `/capture` route installed to the home screen as a PWA (`start_url: /capture`, `display: standalone`) — **not** a native iOS app, since the camera and photo library already work in mobile Safari and what's missing is a phone-shaped surface, not a capability. Reuses `ReceiptService.uploadAndCreate()` behind a queued, immediately-re-arming shutter. Requires a route-group split of `src/routes/+layout.svelte` (auth gate out, nav chrome into `(app)`). Two open risks called out there: **standalone-mode session persistence** (spike before building on it) and **no offline capture on iOS** (Safari has no Background Sync — the one scenario that would justify going native). One on-device check is still outstanding: HEIC is now decoded and transcoded to JPEG like everything else (see [Receipt Image Resize & Zoom](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md)), but nobody has confirmed what an iPhone actually hands over, or that Safari decodes it as expected — if it doesn't, the resize falls back to the original and a large photo is now refused rather than silently uploaded full-size.
 - **Recent-categories dropdown & a11y** _(optional UX, low priority)_. A recent-categories section in the dropdown, a mobile-responsive category dropdown, and category-dropdown ARIA/screen-reader support were specced but never built.
 - **Specced-but-unbuilt UX bits** _(optional, low priority)_. Email-flow vendor auto-assignment (the email path never applies the vendor rule) and the read-only "Rate: 1 EUR = …" text in the receipt edit modal.
 
 ## Bugs / UX issues
 
-- **🔴 Phone photos are rejected by the gate that exists to shrink them — designed, not built.** `uploadAndCreate()` validates the picked file and _then_ resizes it (`ReceiptService.ts:187` → `:191`), so the 5MB limit measures the file the phone handed over rather than the ~400KB JPEG we store: a normal phone photo is refused with "Image too large. Max 5MB." one line before the code that would have fixed it. Designed in [Receipt Image Resize & Zoom](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md) with the governing decision in [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md) — move the gate after resize (25MB pre-decode memory guard), 2400px @ 85%, transcode HEIC and PNG to JPEG (fixing the skipped-HEIC bug below and PNG's never-applied compression), derive the zoom ceiling from each image's natural resolution instead of a flat 400%, delete `/admin/resize-images` (closes **M2**). No backfill needed. Also fixes a doubled decode in `resizeImage` and the wrong MIME passed to OCR.
 - **Receipt with no date is hard to find.** If a receipt has no date it is hard to locate in the receipts view.
 - **Category edit scrolls to top.** When a category is edited we always scroll back up to the top of the window.
 - **Category dropdown clipped.** The category dropdown in the editor window is out of view when clicked.
@@ -44,7 +43,7 @@ reference, not a separate to-do list.
 
 - **🟠 HIGH — unverified, non-unique profile emails allow email-ingestion hijack.** _(Found 2026-07-17 audit; the top open security item.)_ The add-email flow (`src/routes/profile/+page.svelte`) lets a user attach ANY address to their profile (`profiles.email_1..5`) with only format + within-own-profile dedup — **no ownership verification and no cross-user unique constraint**. The Resend webhook attributes inbound receipts via `find_user_by_email(sender)`, which falls through to those profile columns (`resend/handler.ts`). So an attacker can claim a victim's forwarding/secondary address and have the victim's forwarded receipts ingested into the attacker's account (data leak), or make attribution nondeterministic (`limit 1`) when two profiles claim the same address, or pre-claim an address to poison a future user. Not closed by the webhook-signature fix — the abuse is by a legitimately authed user. Fix: confirm ownership via emailed token before an alias participates in lookup; add a global `UNIQUE(lower(email))` (ideally a normalized `profile_emails` table); prefer exact `auth.users` identity over unverified aliases.
 - **Sweep the remaining `SECURITY DEFINER` functions for missing `anon` revokes.** The seed-function lockdown found that `REVOKE … FROM PUBLIC` left a _direct_ `anon` grant in place, needing an explicit `REVOKE … FROM anon`. Only `create_default_hierarchy` / `create_default_categories` were fixed that way. Audit every other `SECURITY DEFINER` function for the same hole and revoke explicitly where `authenticated` is the only legitimate caller.
-- **🟢 LOW / deferred audit items (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` are unauthenticated and SSRF-able via a caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, including svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`); **M2** `/admin/resize-images` is a client-only page that deletes and re-uploads receipt originals with no authz beyond `confirm()` — **slated for deletion**, its one-off migration job is done and re-running it would now destroy detail, see [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md); **M3** the `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding, no limit); **F6** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject — confirm that's intended.
+- **🟢 LOW / deferred audit items (re-verified 2026-07-17).** Unchanged since the 2026-07-05 audit — see the [Security Remediation PRD "Deferred" section](prd-done/prd-security-remediation.md): **H3** `/api/ocr` + `/api/ocr/extract` are unauthenticated and SSRF-able via a caller-supplied `fileUrl` (no auth, no host allow-list — `src/routes/api/ocr/**`); **M1** the Resend webhook still logs full request headers (`resend/handler.ts:334`, including svix signature material) and an API-key prefix/suffix (`:389`); **M3** the `families` INSERT policy is `WITH CHECK (auth.uid() IS NOT NULL)` only (no `created_by` binding, no limit); **F6** `email_send_failures` SELECT is whole-family-scoped, so co-members can read each other's notification recipient + subject — confirm that's intended.

One on-device check is still outstanding: HEIC is now decoded and transcoded to JPEG like everything else (see [Receipt Image Resize & Zoom](plans/2026-08-03-receipt-image-resize-design.md)), but nobody has confirmed what an iPhone actually hands over, or that Safari decodes it as expected — if it doesn't, the resize falls back to the original and a large photo is now refused rather than silently uploaded full-size.
22:- **Specced-but-unbuilt UX bits** _(optional, low priority)_. Email-flow vendor auto-assignment (the email path never applies the vendor rule) and the read-only "Rate: 1 EUR = …" text in the receipt edit modal.
62:- **`insert_receipt_with_context` RPC drops columns.** The RPC inserts only 9 columns and silently omits `suspicious_date` and `exchange_rate_to_cad` (originally `003_insert_receipt_rpc.sql`, carried into the baseline). The Resend email path passes both, so emailed receipts lose their suspicious-date flag and FX rate on the primary path — they survive only if the RPC errors into the direct-insert fallback. Fix: add both columns to the RPC insert in a new migration and confirm the remote function matches.
69:- **Emailed receipts are never resized — the two capture paths store different things.** The Resend handler uploads attachment bytes straight to storage (`supabase/functions/resend/handler.ts:137`) with no size check and no resize, so a receipt forwarded by email is stored at whatever size the sender's mail client produced, while the same receipt uploaded in the browser becomes a 2400px JPEG. Deliberate for now — it is a Deno edge function with no Canvas, so matching it means a WASM image library plus a second copy of the resize rules in `supabase/functions/_shared/` kept in lock-step by hand (the burden CLAUDE.md already flags for the date-correction code), and CPU time inside a webhook that must answer quickly. Recorded as an accepted asymmetry in [ADR-0006](adr/0006-the-stored-image-is-the-contract.md) and the ["Every uploaded image becomes JPEG" invariant](domain-model.md). Revisit if storage cost or emailed-receipt volume grows.

content.text:
Findings, most significant first.

**1. `src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:11` — the accept-list and the transcode-list are two separate literals.**
`IMAGE_TYPES = ['image/jpeg','image/png','image/heic']` sits in the service, `RESIZABLE_TYPES` is an identical private literal in `src/lib/utils/imageResize.ts:25`, and `src/routes/receipts/+page.svelte:492` hardcodes a third copy as `accept="image/jpeg,image/png,image/heic,application/pdf"`. ADR-0006's "every uploaded image becomes JPEG" is now load-bearing (`validateReceiptImage` treats "not PDF" as "is the JPEG we produced"), and that invariant only holds while three unrelated literals happen to agree. The comment on `RESIZABLE_TYPES` even claims it is "the image types the receipts upload control offers", which is an assertion the code does not enforce. Deeper alternative: export one `ACCEPTED_UPLOAD_TYPES` (or `ACCEPTED_IMAGE_TYPES` + `PDF_TYPE`) from `imageResize.ts` — the module that knows what it can transcode — have `validateSourceFile` check against it and the input's `accept` be `ACCEPTED_UPLOAD_TYPES.join(',')`. Then "we accept it" and "we can turn it into the stored contract" are the same fact, and adding webp is one edit instead of three.

**2. `src/lib/utils/imageResize.ts:44` — `toJpegFilename` bends the artifact's name to satisfy a path-builder one layer down.**
`resizeImage` rewrites the File's name (`:141`) purely so `uploadToStorage` (`ReceiptService.ts:278`) — which does `fileToUpload.name.split('.').pop()` — derives `.jpg`. The doc comment states this outright ("so the storage object's extension is not a lie"). The real problem is that the storage path is inferred from a filename when the authoritative fact, `fileToUpload.type`, is already passed to `.upload()` as `contentType` on the very next line. Deeper alternative: derive the extension from the MIME type inside `uploadToStorage` (a two-entry mime→extension map; the repo already has one in `supabase/functions/_shared/attachmentFiltering.ts`), and delete `toJpegFilename`. Then the path is correct for the email path, for PDFs, and for any future format, without every producer having to remember to relabel its output — and `resizeImage` goes back to being purely about pixels. Note `original_filename` (`ReceiptService.ts:336`) already uses the *source* file's name, so the rename serves nothing else.

**3. `src/lib/components/ReceiptImageViewer.svelte:303` — `zoomTo(200, …)` is the flat zoom constant the ADR just removed, still present for double-tap.**
The change replaced `MAX_ZOOM = 400` with a per-image ceiling and moved `MIN_ZOOM`/`ZOOM_STEP` into `imageZoom.ts`, but the double-tap target stayed as a bare `200` inline in the gesture handler. It has exactly the defect the ADR argues against: 200% means a different amount of real detail per device and per image, and on a small receipt it is silently clamped to `maxZoom` rather than being a deliberate stop. Deeper alternative: express the target in `imageZoom.ts` alongside the other limits — e.g. `calculateDoubleTapZoom(maxZoom)` returning `maxZoom` (double-tap to true resolution) or a midpoint derived from it — so every zoom destination in the viewer comes from the same per-image derivation, and the component holds no zoom percentages at all.

**4. `src/lib/services/ReceiptService.ts:31` — `shrunk: boolean` conflates "not applicable" with "the shrink failed", and the gate only survives it by ordering.**
`prepareFileForUpload` returns `shrunk: false` for both a PDF pass-through (`:259`) and a resize failure (`:269`); `validateReceiptImage` produces the right message only because it returns early on `file.type === PDF_TYPE` (`:209`) before reaching the `shrunk` branch. The reason for rejection is thrown away at the point where it is known and reconstructed from a boolean at the point where it is needed. It also couples to finding 1: any accepted-but-non-resizable image type would get "This image could not be shrunk" when in fact nothing was attempted. Deeper alternative: make the preparation outcome explicit — `{ file, outcome: 'transcoded' | 'stored-as-received' | 'shrink-failed' }` — and let `validateReceiptImage` map outcome to message. The PDF special case in the gate then disappears, because "stored as received" is a first-class outcome rather than a type check.

**5. `src/lib/components/ReceiptImageViewer.svelte:93` — the viewport box that *defines* 100% is a magic pair, duplicated against the CSS that enforces it.**
`calculateFitDimensions` was correctly extracted and parameterised, but its arguments `window.innerWidth * 0.9, window.innerHeight * 0.8` must agree with `max-width: 90vw; max-height: 80vh` written literally at `:481` and `:482`. Since `MIN_ZOOM` is now *defined* as "fit to viewport", these numbers are part of the zoom contract yet live in two representations (JS math and CSS strings) that nothing keeps in sync. Deeper alternative: a single `VIEWPORT_FRACTION = { width: 0.9, height: 0.8 }` (in `imageZoom.ts`, next to the definition of what 100% means) used both to compute the fit and to emit the container's max-width/max-height, so the ceiling arithmetic and the box that clips it cannot drift.

**6. `.claude/settings.local.json:215-218` — single-use scratch commands persisted into the project allowlist.**
The diff adds permanent permission entries for `cp src/lib/components/ReceiptImageViewer.svelte /tmp/riv.bak`, a `perl -pi -e` that rewrites the `maxZoom` line of that specific file back to `400`, `rm /tmp/riv.bak`, and `python3 -`. These are the mutation-test scaffolding for this change, not durable capabilities; keeping them grants a standing write-capable `perl -pi` / `python3 -` allowance and grows a shared config with per-task entries. Deeper alternative: drop the four entries; if mutation-checking the zoom ceiling is worth repeating, it belongs as a test, not as a permission grant for an ad-hoc in-place edit.

Nothing else in the diff looked shallow to me: moving the gate to `validateReceiptImage`, the `MAX_SOURCE_MB` memory guard as an explicitly different kind of limit, hoisting resize+validation out of `withRetry`, `calculateMaxZoom` living in `imageZoom.ts` rather than the component, and deleting `/admin/resize-images` outright instead of updating it are all fixes at the level the ADR argues for. `MAX_IMAGE_DIMENSION`/`IMAGE_QUALITY` are now defaults on `resizeImage` with a single caller passing nothing, which is the right single home.
